newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks trim losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks trim losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks clawed back some ground and closed slightly lower Monday in threadlike trading.

"The market was barely alive today," said Miguel Daneri at traders Boston Securities. "The Jewish holiday and the prevailing sense of caution ahead of tomorrow's (U.S.) Federal Reserve talks made for a very dull session."

The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV followed through on Friday's mild correction with a 0.5 percent drop to 545.18, while floor volume shrank to a miserly 5.5 million pesos from Friday's already very weak tally of 12.2 million.
Traders said the bolsa was expecting a quarter-point rise in the U.S. Federal Funds rate to 5.5 percent Tuesday by the Federal Open Market Committee.

"A small increase could actually benefit the markets, because most are in line for a (downward) correction and this could be the perfect excuse," said Daneri. "I think after the initial drop many investors would consider the prices as a buying opportunity."
Dealers warned the scenario could be different, however, if the Fed raised rates by half a point.
Otherwise the undertone of the bolsa is firm thanks to good economic indicators, notwithstanding a 36-hour general strike scheduled to start at midday Thursday, dealers said.

The economic think-tank FIEL reported earlier Monday industrial production grew 9.2 percent in August compared to the same month of 1995, while the government announced after the market close that the public sector deficit excluding privatization income shrank to $203.4 million in August from $833.6 million in July.
In the session the broad market dipped 0.2 percent, with losers beating winners 23 to 12 and 17 issues ending flat.
Over-the-counter volume dwindled to 32 million pesos from 70.1 million Friday.

Worst main-tier performances were by real estate developer Irsa, which slid 2.7 percent, power utility Central Puerto and construction stock Juan Minetti, both off 2.1 percent, and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, down 1.8 percent.
Top gainers were petrochemical concern Ipako, construction stock Polledo and agricultural holding company Cresud, which added 2.8 percent, 1.1 percent and 0.6 percent, respectively.
